stem:
Students plan to investigate the different states of matter. They will measure the volume of water in three containers after five days. They make this table to organize the data.

| Container | Volume of Water (beginning) | Temperature of Water (beginning) | Location of Container                                 | Volume of Water (after five days) |
|-----------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| 1         | 200 mL                      | 24°C                            | Inside a refrigerator                                  | ?                                 |
| 2         | 200 mL                      | 24°C                            | On a desk in front of low-speed fan                    | ?                                 |
| 3         | 200 mL                      | 24°C                            | On a sunny windowsill in front of an opened window    | ?                                 |

Which graph represents the volume of water most likely left in the containers after five days?

options.label: A
options.text: Graph showing Container 1 = 200 mL, Container 2 = 100 mL, Container 3 = 150 mL

options.label: B
options.text: Graph showing Container 1 = 190 mL, Container 2 = 150 mL, Container 3 = 120 mL

options.label: C
options.text: Graph showing Container 1 = 200 mL, Container 2 = 210 mL, Container 3 = 220 mL

options.label: D
options.text: Graph showing Container 1 = 150 mL, Container 2 = 200 mL, Container 3 = 50 mL

visual_elements: Table with container information and volumes
Four bar graphs labeled A, B, C, D depicting volume of water for containers 1, 2, 3
notes: The problem is a typical volume measurement and evaporation experiment; options correspond exactly to images provided.
